Bachelors degree in the life sciences or related discipline (and/or equivalent education and experience) (Preferred)
Research experience in microbiology or molecular biology and a strong understanding of the underlying scientific principles
Prior research experience in bacterial genetics

In this position, the Laboratory Research Assistant supports the Seed Lab in the Department of Plant and Microbial Biology at UC Berkeley, which investigates the interactions between phages and Vibrio cholerae. The Laboratory Research Assistant carries out the isolation and sequencing of phages and V. cholerae, including screening samples by PCR and extracting DNA for next-generation sequencing. This position performs phenotypic assays to assess phage infectivity and utilizes molecular genetics to engineer phages and V. cholerae mutants. Additionally, the Laboratory Research Assistant maintains lab organization, manages consumable and reagent inventories, handles ordering, and ensures accurate documentation of experimental results.
Isolate and purify phages and Vibrio cholerae, Isolate genomic DNA from phages and Vibrio cholerae for whole genome sequencing
Perform PCR to screen for phages and Vibrio cholerae
Maintain a well-organized collection of phages and Vibrio cholerae from samples, including electronic records
Perform phenotypic assays to evaluate phage infectivity and susceptibility of V. cholerae to phage infection
Construct bacterial and phage mutants
Maintenance of laboratory consumable and reagent inventories
Ordering for the lab operations
Participate in lab meetings to keep abreast of current research projects and support needs
Present summary of findings verbally at lab meetings and in written format if findings are gauged to be appropriate for publication
Proficiency in data management
Ability to work both independently and as a team member
Ability to maintain an organized record of experiments
Ability to communicate effectively in oral and written form
